natural: throw away like an old shoe

meaning.en: To cast something or someone aside without a second thought, as if it were worthless.
meaning.zh: 像扔掉破鞋一样丢弃，毫不可惜。

equivalents: cast aside like an old shoe

examples.zh: 他功成名就后，把当年的患难之交弃如敝屣。
examples.en: Once successful, he cast off the friends who had stood by him like old shoes.

examples.zh: 她把别人视若珍宝的奖章弃如敝屣。
examples.en: She tossed aside the medal others would treasure as if it were junk.

story.en: Mencius says the sage-king Shun would have abandoned the whole empire as lightly as discarding a worn-out shoe (舜视弃天下犹弃敝蹝也).
story.zh: 《孟子》：“舜视弃天下犹弃敝蹝也。”

usage.en: Usually describes dropping people, honours or principles one ought to value; often critical. Written style; 敝屣 is also read bì xǐ, not bì shǐ.
usage.zh: 多含贬义，常指抛弃本应珍视的人或事物，书面语。“屣”读xǐ。

meaning.en: Officials sent into exile and men of letters; refers to poets and scholars who write with a melancholy, wandering spirit.
meaning.zh: 指被贬谪流放的官员和失意的文人墨客。

examples.zh: 岳阳楼上，迁客骚人留下了许多千古名篇。
examples.en: On Yueyang Tower, exiled officials and poets left behind many timeless works.

examples.zh: 这座古亭自古便是迁客骚人登临抒怀之处。
examples.en: This old pavilion has long been where banished literati climbed to pour out their feelings.

story.en: In 'Yueyang Tower', Fan Zhongyan writes that exiled officials and poets often gathered here, and their feelings on seeing the view varied (迁客骚人，多会于此，览物之情，得无异乎).
story.zh: “迁客骚人，多会于此，览物之情，得无异乎？”

usage.en: Literary; a collective noun for people, often used in descriptions of scenic spots.
usage.zh: 文学色彩浓，指一类人，常用于介绍名胜古迹。

meaning.en: Unable to sleep peacefully because of worry or anxiety.
meaning.zh: 睡觉也睡不安稳，形容心中忧虑不安。

examples.zh: 公司资金链出了问题，他连日来寝不安席。
examples.en: With the company's cash flow in trouble, he has barely slept these days.

examples.zh: 孩子高烧不退，母亲寝不安席守了一夜。
examples.en: The child's fever would not go down, and the mother kept anxious watch all night.

usage.en: Used as a predicate, usually with 食不甘味 (food has no taste). Written style.
usage.zh: 多作谓语，常与“食不甘味”连用，书面语。

literal: Swallow (Zhao Feiyan) · slim · Jade Ring (Yang Yuhuan) · plump

meaning.en: Beauties of different types, each with her own charm; also used for varied styles of art that are each admirable.
meaning.zh: 赵飞燕体态苗条，杨玉环体态丰腴，各有各的美。比喻女子形态各异而各有特色，也比喻艺术风格不同而各有所长。

equivalents: each beauty has her own charm

examples.zh: 展厅里的仕女图燕瘦环肥，各具风姿。
examples.en: The paintings of court ladies on show are slim or full-figured, each with her own grace.

examples.zh: 这两位画家风格迥异，可谓燕瘦环肥，各擅胜场。
examples.en: The two painters have very different styles, like slim Feiyan and plump Yuhuan, each excelling in their own way.

origin.source: 苏轼《孙莘老求墨妙亭诗》

story.en: Su Shi writes that with calligraphy, as with beauties, 'long and short, plump and thin each have their charm; Yuhuan and Feiyan alike have turned to dust' (短长肥瘦各有态，玉环飞燕皆尘土).
story.zh: “短长肥瘦各有态，玉环飞燕皆尘土。”

usage.en: Often the order is 环肥燕瘦 as well; treat as one expression. Praises variety; do not use it to describe a person's actual weight.
usage.zh: 也作“环肥燕瘦”。含褒义，强调各有千秋，不用来评价具体体型。

meaning.en: Someone who corrects a single word in your writing, and so counts as your teacher.
meaning.zh: 指能给自己改正一个字的人，是自己的老师；形容善于炼字、虚心求教。

equivalents: the one who fixes a word and earns the title of teacher
a teacher for a single word

examples.zh: 编辑改动的那个动词恰到好处，真是我的一字之师。
examples.en: The verb the editor changed was just right; truly a teacher to me for that one word.

examples.zh: 他谦虚好学，常把指出错别字的读者称作一字之师。
examples.en: Modest and eager to learn, he often calls readers who point out typos his teachers for a word.

story.en: The monk-poet Qi Ji showed Zheng Gu his poem 'Early Plum'; Zheng Gu changed 'several branches bloomed' (数枝开) to 'one branch bloomed' (一枝开), and Qi Ji bowed to him as 'my teacher for a single word'.
story.zh: 相传齐己《早梅》诗有“前村深雪里，昨夜数枝开”，郑谷改“数”为“一”，齐己拜为“一字师”。

usage.en: Respectful; usually used about the person who corrected you. Often in the pattern 某人是我的一字之师.
usage.zh: 含敬意，多指为自己改正字句的人，常说“是我的一字之师”。

meaning.en: Benefits that reach and help many later generations.
meaning.zh: 恩泽遍及后代，指功德影响深远。

examples.zh: 都江堰的修建泽被后世，至今仍灌溉着成都平原。
examples.en: Building the Dujiangyan benefited all later ages and still irrigates the Chengdu Plain.

examples.zh: 这位医学家的研究泽被后世。
examples.en: This physician's research has benefited generations to come.

usage.en: Praise for great works or deeds; formal. 泽 = favour, blessing, not 'pond'.
usage.zh: 褒义，多用于评价功绩，书面语。“泽”指恩惠。

meaning.en: A vicious, cruel nature, like a snake or scorpion.
meaning.zh: 像毒蛇、蝎子一样狠毒的心肠，形容人心肠狠毒。

examples.zh: 看似温柔的继母，竟是蛇蝎心肠。
examples.en: The seemingly gentle stepmother turned out to have a heart of venom.

examples.zh: 别被她的笑脸骗了，她可是个蛇蝎心肠的女人。
examples.en: Don't be fooled by her smile; she is a malicious woman.

usage.en: Strongly derogatory; describes character, usually of a woman in older texts but fine for anyone. Often 蛇蝎美人 for a dangerous beauty.
usage.zh: 贬义强烈，形容人品，常说“蛇蝎心肠的人”。

meaning.en: To stir up trouble where there was none, or make a fuss over nothing.
meaning.zh: 没有风却掀起波浪，比喻无事生非，凭空制造事端。

equivalents: make a storm in a teacup

examples.zh: 两家本来相安无事，是他无风起浪，挑拨离间。
examples.en: The two families were getting along until he stirred up trouble out of nothing.

examples.zh: 这件事纯属无风起浪，大家不必当真。
examples.en: This is a fuss over nothing; don't take it seriously.

usage.en: Derogatory when aimed at a person; also used neutrally for a baseless rumour. Close to 无事生非, which is more common.
usage.zh: 多含贬义，指无中生有的是非。比“无事生非”略少用。

literal: form · same as · empty · set up

meaning.en: Existing in name only and serving no real purpose, as if it were not there.
meaning.zh: 虽然设置了，但起不到应有作用，如同摆设。

equivalents: for show only, serving no purpose

examples.zh: 门口的监控摄像头早就坏了，形同虚设。
examples.en: The camera at the entrance has long been broken and is just for show.

examples.zh: 规定再多，没人执行也形同虚设。
examples.en: However many rules there are, they are meaningless if nobody enforces them.

usage.en: Predicate; criticises rules, equipment or posts that do not work. Common in news and essays.
usage.zh: 作谓语，批评制度、设施等不起作用，常见于新闻和作文。

meaning.en: Evil people and wicked practices; originally Buddhist terms for demons and non-Buddhist teachings.
meaning.zh: 原为佛教用语，指邪恶的鬼怪和不正当的学说；现泛指各种坏人和歪门邪道。

examples.zh: 他不好好工作，一心想靠邪魔外道发财。
examples.en: He doesn't work properly and hopes to get rich by shady ways.

examples.zh: 我们要警惕各种邪魔外道，不要上当受骗。
examples.en: We must be wary of all manner of charlatans and cults and not be fooled.

usage.en: Derogatory; for bad people or crooked methods. In speech, often jokey or exaggerated.
usage.zh: 含贬义，指坏人或歪门邪道，口语中常带夸张戏谑。

meaning.en: To secretly give someone advance news or a warning, usually so they can act in time.
meaning.zh: 暗中把消息透露给有关的人。

examples.zh: 有人给嫌疑人通风报信，警方扑了个空。
examples.en: Someone tipped off the suspect, and the police found nothing.

examples.zh: 听说老板要来检查，小李赶紧给同事通风报信。
examples.en: Hearing the boss was coming to inspect, Xiao Li quickly gave his colleagues a heads-up.

usage.en: Neutral to negative depending on whose side you take; usually a verb phrase with 给/向. Casual.
usage.zh: 视立场褒贬，常作谓语，口语色彩。

meaning.en: Natural disasters and man-made calamities; misfortunes of every kind.
meaning.zh: 自然灾害和人为的祸患，泛指各种灾难。

examples.zh: 连年的天灾人祸使这个地区民不聊生。
examples.en: Years of natural and man-made disasters left the region's people destitute.

examples.zh: 保险可以在一定程度上抵御天灾人祸带来的损失。
examples.en: Insurance can offset, to some extent, losses from natural and man-made disasters.

usage.en: Common in news and essays; a noun phrase, subject or object.
usage.zh: 多作主语、宾语，常见于新闻和作文。

meaning.en: To get a battle or task over quickly and settle it at once.
meaning.zh: 迅速作战，迅速解决战斗；也指尽快把事情办完。

examples.zh: 对手实力强，我们只能速战速决。
examples.en: The opponent is strong, so we can only try to win fast.

examples.zh: 这件事不宜拖，咱们速战速决吧。
examples.en: This shouldn't drag on; let's get it done fast.

usage.en: Neutral; both military and everyday use, as predicate. Opposite of 持久战 in strategy.
usage.zh: 中性，军事和日常均可，作谓语。

meaning.en: A dense crowd of people moving about; a packed, bustling scene.
meaning.zh: 许多人聚在一起，人头聚集晃动，形容人多拥挤热闹。

examples.zh: 节假日的景区门口人头攒动。
examples.en: At holiday times the scenic area's gate is packed with people.

examples.zh: 演唱会现场人头攒动，热闹非凡。
examples.en: The concert venue was a teeming crowd, lively beyond words.

usage.en: Descriptive, often a predicate after a place word. Note 攒 is read cuán here (gather), not zǎn (save).
usage.zh: 多作谓语，描写场景。“攒”此处读cuán，不读zǎn。

meaning.en: Warm, gentle spring weather and bright, beautiful scenery.
meaning.zh: 春风和煦，阳光明媚，形容春天天气晴好、景色明丽。

examples.zh: 春和景明，正是出门踏青的好时节。
examples.en: With the mild weather and bright scenery, it's a fine time for an outing.

examples.zh: 三月的江南春和景明，花开满城。
examples.en: In March, the south of the Yangtze is bright and mild, with flowers across the city.

story.en: Fan Zhongyan describes a fine spring day on the lake: 'when spring is mild and the scene is bright, the waves are calm' (至若春和景明，波澜不惊，上下天光，一碧万顷).
story.zh: “至若春和景明，波澜不惊，上下天光，一碧万顷。”

usage.en: Literary, scenery description; only for spring. Often appears in essays and greetings.
usage.zh: 文学色彩浓，只形容春天，常用于写景。

literal: deep green · emerald · about to · drip

meaning.en: A deep, fresh green so rich that it seems about to drip from the leaves.
meaning.zh: 青绿的颜色浓得好像要滴下来，形容草木青翠茂盛。

examples.zh: 雨后的竹林苍翠欲滴。
examples.en: After the rain, the bamboo grove is a lush, dripping green.

examples.zh: 山坡上的茶树苍翠欲滴，让人心旷神怡。
examples.en: The tea bushes on the slope are so richly green that they refresh the spirit.

usage.en: Descriptive predicate or attributive for plants, hills, leaves; positive.
usage.zh: 描写植物、山林，作谓语或定语，褒义。

meaning.en: A long-standing bad habit that is hard to break.
meaning.zh: 长期养成的坏习惯很难改掉。

examples.zh: 他赌瘾上来，积习难改，又去了牌桌。
examples.en: His gambling craving returned; unable to shake the old habit, he went back to the card table.

examples.zh: 拖延症是积习难改，但并非没有办法。
examples.en: Procrastination is a stubborn habit, but not hopeless.

usage.en: Predicate; the habit is bad (积习 is a bad habit). Often with 本性难移.
usage.zh: 作谓语，“积习”指坏习惯，常与“本性难移”连用。

synonyms: 狗改不了吃屎——本性难移

natural: a thousand gullies, ten thousand ravines

meaning.en: Terrain cut by countless gullies and ravines; rugged, broken land.
meaning.zh: 形容地表沟壑纵横，地形复杂崎岖。

examples.zh: 黄土高原千沟万壑，交通十分不便。
examples.en: The Loess Plateau is furrowed with gullies and travel is difficult.

examples.zh: 飞机下方是千沟万壑的山区。
examples.en: Below the plane lay mountains cut by countless ravines.

usage.en: Descriptive attributive or predicate for terrain, esp. the Loess Plateau. Also used jokingly of a deeply wrinkled face.
usage.zh: 描写地形，常用于黄土高原。

meaning.en: To treat something with cold indifference and pay it no attention.
meaning.zh: 冷淡地对待，不加理睬，毫不关心。

examples.zh: 面对群众的意见，他竟漠然置之。
examples.en: Faced with the public's complaints, he simply ignored them.

examples.zh: 别人的劝告，他一概漠然置之。
examples.en: He brushes aside all advice from others.

usage.en: Critical; the object is something that should matter. Often shortened to 置之不理 in speech.
usage.zh: 含贬义，对象本应重视的事，多为书面语。

meaning.en: A wish that livestock thrive; the farm and household prosper.
meaning.zh: 家养牲畜繁殖旺盛，多用于祝愿农家兴旺。

examples.zh: 春联写着“五谷丰登，六畜兴旺”。
examples.en: The Spring Festival couplet reads: 'Bumper crops and thriving livestock'.

examples.zh: 乡亲们祝愿新年六畜兴旺，家家富足。
examples.en: The villagers wish the new year brings thriving livestock and prosperity to every home.

usage.en: The six animals are horse, ox, sheep, pig, dog, chicken. Often paired with 五谷丰登; a New Year wish.
usage.zh: 六畜指马牛羊猪狗鸡。常与“五谷丰登”连用，多作新年祝愿。

meaning.en: An ideal, well-matched marriage, as precious as gold and jade.
meaning.zh: 指美满而理想的姻缘，常指婚姻美满。

examples.zh: 这对新人才貌相当，真是金玉良缘。
examples.en: The couple are well matched in looks and talent, a perfect marriage.

examples.zh: 祝你们金玉良缘，白头偕老。
examples.en: May yours be a perfect match, and may you grow old together.

usage.en: Used as a wedding wish or praise. In the novel Dream of the Red Chamber it refers to the match of the 金 (Baochai's locket) and 玉 (Baoyu's jade), so it can carry a poignant note.
usage.zh: 常用于婚礼祝福。《红楼梦》中指宝玉的玉与宝钗的金锁相配之说。

natural: used to it, no longer startled

meaning.en: Having seen something so often that it no longer surprises or alarms.
meaning.zh: 看惯了就不觉得奇怪，不再吃惊。

examples.zh: 北京的堵车，司机们早已见惯不惊。
examples.en: Drivers are long used to Beijing's traffic jams and no longer react.

examples.zh: 他在急诊室工作多年，对生死见惯不惊。
examples.en: After years in the emergency room, he takes life and death in stride.

usage.en: Neutral; can hint that numbness is a bit worrying. Often paired with 司空见惯.
usage.zh: 中性，有时暗含“麻木”之意，常与“司空见惯”并用。

meaning.en: To start something but not finish it.
meaning.zh: 有开头，没结尾，指做事不能坚持到底。

examples.zh: 他做事总是有头无尾，让人不放心。
examples.en: He always leaves things half done, which makes people uneasy.

examples.zh: 这个项目有头无尾，最后不了了之。
examples.en: The project had a start but no ending and fizzled out.

usage.en: Criticism of work habits; predicate or attributive. Opposite 有始有终.
usage.zh: 批评做事不坚持，作谓语、定语。与“有始有终”相反。

meaning.en: One's personal opinion, often offered modestly as only a private view.
meaning.zh: 个人的见解或意见，常作谦辞。

examples.zh: 以上只是我的一己之见，供大家参考。
examples.en: The above is only my own view, for everyone's reference.

examples.zh: 不能凭一己之见就下结论。
examples.en: You can't draw conclusions from just your own view.

usage.en: Polite when used for oneself; with 凭/拘于 it can criticise narrowness.
usage.zh: 自称时为谦辞；与“凭”“囿于”搭配时可含批评意味。
